देसी स्टाइल पाव भाजी/Desi Style Paav Bhaji 🇮🇳 ❤️ 🏠 ❤️🏠❤️🏠❤️🏠❤️
_______
Good Afternoon Instafamily ❤️
_______
क्या आप को पाव भाजी पसन्द हैं?😍
लाइक एंड कॉमेंट करके बतायें😋😍
_______
Ingredients:
_______
8-10 Potatoes
1 Cauliflower 
2-3 Carrot
1 Cup Peas
3 Cups Water
4 tbsp oil
1 tbsp Ginger Garlic Paste
2 Onions - Finely Chopped 
3 Tomatoes - Finaly Chopped 
1 tbsp Red Chilli Powder 
1 tbsp Kashmiri Red Chilli
2-3 tbsp Pav Bhaji Masala
Salt to Taste
Coriander to Garnish
_______
Recipe:
_______
- Pressure cook roughly chopped potatoes, cauliflower, carrot & peas with 3 cups of water to 3 whistles. - Mash the boiled veggies & keep them aside. - Heat oil in a wok. - Add ginger garlic paste & cook till aroma fades away. - Add onions & cook till turn light brown. - Add tomatoes & cook till corner leaves oil. - Add red chilli powder, kashmiri chilli powder, pav bhaji masala & mix. - Add mashed veggies & salt.  Mix and cook for 7-8 mints. * Adjust consistency by adding water. - Stir & mash veggies in between. - Garnish with coriander.
- Serve hot with pav.
______

Need another reason to love pav bhaji? Well, we bring you the amazing Leftover Pav Bhaji Bread Pakoda
.
.
.
Ingredients
•	Bread - 2 slices •	Butter- 20 g
•	Lehsun chutney – 25 g
For the stuffing •	Pav bhaji - 60 g (Per sandwich)
•	Onion circles – 10 g
For batter coating •	Besan – 30 g •	Water – 50ml •	Salt – To taste (As per required)
•	Roasted sesame seeds – 5 g
•	Pinch of Hing- 1 g
•	Pinch of Baking soda – 1 g
•	Red chili powder – ¼ tsp •	Coriander sprig - 1

Procedure
•	For making the batter add the besan, salt, turmeric powder, baking soda and red chili powder in a bowl.  Add in some water and whisk it thoroughly to get the batter in smooth consistency.
•	Using the fresh bread apply butter and lehsun chutney to it on both breads.
•	Now with the help of spoon or spatula put a dollop of leftover pav bhaji in the center of bread. (Make sure that the pav bhaji is reduced to a thick consistency & is at room temperature).
•	Spread evenly on all the sides of bread ascending with onion circles.
•	Now place the other bread making a sandwich.
•	Cut the bread sandwich twice forming 4 triangles.
•	Heat oil on moderate temperature (130 – 150 degrees)
•	Dip the sandwiches in the besan batter and fry them till the sandwiches turn golden brown. •	Once ready, garnish with chopped onion, coriander, chaat masala.
•	Serve with some lehsun chutney
.
.
.

Tawa pulao  _ is a famous Mumbai street food .It is an easy rice item which you can quickly prepare on tawa .I came across this recipe in Tarladalal's cook book. *You can prepare this recipe with left over rice too.
*Once the chopping is done ,pulao gets ready in minutes.
*Do not over cook the vegetables.Its should be crispy .
*Add any veggies of your choice.
* I have used beans,carrot ,capsicum,green peas,paneer.You can include baby corn,cauliflower,potatoes.

Paying homage to the 20th century Iranian Cafés of Mumbai, Dishoom showcases the old school welcoming themes of jazz music, coupled with food that strikes a cord with every Indian that crosses the majestic doorway. 
As you enter, you are greeted by old school jukeboxes, Parsi themed decor, stained glass lamps and a friendly server that leads you to an inviting booth. 
The bottomless Masala Chai served in the iconic Railway glasses does justice to India's drink of choice over biscuits. It has the perfect hit of ginger, with overtones of Cloves and Cardamom. 
Ditching the shortcrust for Filo, the Lamb and Vegetable Samosas are served with a side of Mint, Tamarind and Tomato Chutneys, the perfect combination for the savoury stuffed flaky pastry to contrast with the sourness of the dipping sauces. 
The Okra fries marinated with traditional blends of Indian spices are little munchies that kids seem to wipe off plates in no time. 
To end with, I tried the Keema Pav. Undoubtedly the BEST I have ever tried. Made from lamb mince that is slowly stewed in a mixture of flavoursome spices, oil and onions, the Keema is a smooth curry that is scooped up in freshly baked buns toasted with Desi Ghee. An experience that can not be explained to its full depth of flavours and emotions. 
Unquestionably the deserving recipient of Yelp's Best restaurant award for 3 years in a row.

• Pav Bhaji is popular Indian street food where dinner rolls/buns are served with spicy mashed veggies topped with dollop of butter. Street food doesn’t get better than this!
• This Pav Bhaji Recipe is spicy, so flavorful and can be easily made vegan by replacing butter with vegan butter! If you have never had pav bhaji in your life, you are seriously missing out!
Indian street food is my favorite kind of food. It’s something that I can eat everyday and still not get bored of it.
• Ever since I can remember, I have been a huge pav bhaji fan. You can find it pretty much everywhere in India but if you want to taste the best pav bhaji , go to Mumbai! That’s where this dish originated from and the one at Juhu Beach is so good, trust me!
I ate pav bhaji all my life but can still not forget the one I had in Mumbai. ▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪▪

So this special dish was prepared yesterday evening and is dedicated to all those vegetarians out there! Known on Indian streets as Pav Bhaji, its a medley of steamed vegetables, mashed and cooked with onions, tomatoes and peppers on slow fire with a mix of spice powders, fresh ginger-garlic and with a generous dollop of butter! The best way to enjoy this is with grilled and buttered pav or burger like buns and some fresh onion slices on the side. If you like it spicy, like I do, add lots of fresh green chillies and dry red chillies into the bhaji dish. 
It always takes me back to my university days in Pune (a town outside Mumbai) where this dish was readily available at our university canteen, road side stalls and all fast food restaurants. #foodmemories #food #pavbhaji #homemade #cookingclass #cookery #cooking #indianfood #surreyfood #muddystilettos #goodfood #surrey #vegetarian #eat #delicious #foodie😋 #streetfood #spices #curry

Yesterday's post by Radhika (@ticklingpalates) made me crave for pav bhaji. So today I decided to make everything from scratch. As I started the process, the bottle of yeast started throwing a tantrum. It just wouldn't open. Tried all possible, known ways but it wouldn't budge. Maybe the yeast was angry that I hardly bake bread 😂😂😂 So got the store bought pav buns and made a home style bhaji with spice level suited to our tastes. Hubby as usual "paneerified" it. 😜😜😜 A few days back, I was telling him, "do you know there is a type of diet where you can eat paneer every single day?". He got so excited, "now that's the kind of diet I like". Before he started to jump around, I had to break the tough news, "but you can't have any chapathis to go with it". The excitement fizzled out like a diwali cracker. 😆😆😆 People who follow THAT diet, please don't take any offence 😊

What’s the best breakfast dish in the world? Is it the UK’s full English? America’s waffles and pancakes? France’s croissants and jams? China’s dim sum and dumplings? Or Japan’s rice, fish and miso soup? .
No, it’s an Indian dish by way of Portugal – Pav Bhaji. .
Menus often describe Pav Bhaji as “tangy mashed potato with Indian spices served with soft rolls”. With this in mind, you wont be shocked to hear that the dish is a potato based curry served with toasted soft bread rolls. .
The addition of the onions and lemon juice makes the dish. Cutting through the spice, they produce a mouth-watering combination of tangy umami and spices. So good is the Bhaji that there’s no need for the Pav, other than to bulk the dish out. .
Pav, Portuguese in origin (a literal translation being bread), are soft white rolls, while Bhaji is a vegetable curry from the Indian state of Maharashtra. The breakfast was born when Pav were introduced as a pairing for the Bhaji by the Portuguese when they controlled Maharashtra. .
Now my go-to breakfast when I'm in India, I’ve had multiple versions. In Jodhpur, I even came across a lamb mince version, but not even that could live up to the memory of the first one I had at Udaipur’s Lake Palace hotel @tajlakepalace . If you see this dish on a menu I can’t encourage you enough to try it, and be liberal with the shallots and lemon/lime or you’ll miss out. .

#pavbhaji #foodgram #foodgasm #soulfood #foodislife #foodstagram #foodphotography #raipurfoodie #raipurfood #indianfood #indianfoodblogger #likeforlike #foodblogger #foodblog #veganfood #connoisseur #connoisseurvista #raipur #bhilai #durg #chhattisgarh #india

A world-famous fast food dish or perhaps the king of the street food from the western state of Maharashtra - Pav Bhaji is an amalgamation of vegetables gingered up with a unique blend of spices served with soft bread roll. Having originated during the thriving textile industry business in Mumbai, 
Pav Bhaji was invented as a midnight dish by street food vendors, made with all the leftover vegetables from the day, mashed up together, with loads of added spice, and butter. Bhaji is the Marathi word for a vegetable dish, and pav probably comes from the Portuguese word for bread. A mixture of vegetables mashed into a rich red-orange coloured spice mixture. Pav Bhaji is a flavourful combination of spicy and tangy, and is eaten with raw onions, a squeeze of lime and a dollop of butter.... .

We just couldn't resist some hot spicy Pav Bhaji!! 😍😋
. 
Checked out this small restaurant in Lower Parel named 'Status'. This one is quite famous for its Pani Puri (also popularly known as GolGappa). Since we had already tried the Pani Puri here a couple of times, we decided to check in & try their Pav Bhaji (it was actually the irresistible smell of the hot Pav Bhaji that drew us in). We ordered Cheese Pav Bhaji (Rs 110) along with Jain Pav Bhaji (Rs 95). The Bhaji was served really hot & also the Pav (a type of Indian bread) was soft and melted butter was spread on top of it. Both the Jain & Cheese version of the Bhajis were decent in taste. Although the smell is really tempting, the Pav Bhaji didn't really live up to our expectations. However, it was definitely worth a try!!
. 
Our rating:
Ambience - 🤩🤩
Food - 🤩🤩🤩
Overall - 2.5/5
.

Tomorrow is our first day to school!
Sidd is stepping into second grade and Sahana is starting her journey into elementary school as TK-er. For the summer we packed their days with summer camps, garden projects, house cleaning & closet / toy organizing, vacation to Canada and couple of day/ weekend trips around Bay Area. For the last 10 days we kept them home to watch TV, nap, dig some dirt , build a pond in the backyard and just do nothing. They woke up in their own pace, ate when they wanted and played until they were tired. Overall a great summer 2018 to remember and cherish.

Homemade Pav Bhaji is the best for a Sunday!  Added with extra butter and  some lemon...It totally makes my day !
Ingredients:-
1) Potatoes - 2
2) Cauliflower - half
3) Carrot - half 
4) Chopped Onion and Capsicum - according to ur taste
5) Chopped Tomatoes - 3
6) Grated garlic - 10
7) Green Peas 
8) Pav Bhaji Masala , Salt to taste , Kashmiri red chilli powder - All 2-3 tsp.
. :Steps and Procedure :-
1. Boil the veggies in a pressure cooker for 2 whistles on medium flame and keep the water left after the boiling in separate container. 
2. Mash all the veggies. Now heat a pan and add some butter n oil to it. Then add green chilli , ginger,garlic and fry it for a minute on medium flame.

3. Then add onions to the mixture and fry till soft and turning yellow. Stir nicely.

4. Add Chopped Capsicum and green peas . Mix it and fry for again a min after which u can add the tomatoes and stir it carefully.

5. Add some salt to taste and fry for 3-4 mins . After this , add kashmiri red chilli powder and pavbhaji masala to it .

6. Cover the pan and let it simmer for 30 - 40 sec so that all masalas get roasted well . At this point , add mashed veggies and mix well. 
KEEP MASHING THE BHAJI FOR THAT RICH FLAVOUR 
7. Now add some water which u kept separately and stir for sometime. Again add very less salt. 
8. Now  stir the mixture and cover the pan to let it simmer for 2-3 mins. It's Ready!........Add some butter and coriander leaves for the extra delicious flavour.
Don't Forget to add lemon too!! 9. Toast the pavs with butter and SERVE HOT with some chopped onions!! Thank me later 😂
.

Amul butter Pav Bhaji at Sardar Refreshments, Tardeo 💯 
Detailed elucidation of why Sardar is iconic:
(1) The heavenly smell that hits you even before you can spot the mosambi garlanded facade.
Who needs google maps when you can follow the delicious smelling buttery goodness, no?
(2) You get two choices either you decide to get fat (Amul Pav Bhaji) or very fat (Cheese Butter Pav Bhaji).
Even breathing the butter laden air around makes you fat!
Strict no diet policy.
(3) They have been serving Pav Bhaji since 1960’s and they say the taste hasn’t changed!

And did I mention the butter? ✨

No matter how many times you eat pav bhaji, you’ll still drool over it when you pass a pav bhaji vendor 💕
Every place that serves this street food, loved by all Indians (which I m sure of) has a unique taste given to it. It can be the difference in the way they prepare it or the ingredients that vary.. but, every time I have it, I just happen to love it more🤪

Here's to one such place in Pune, that serves one of the best of the #PavBhaji in the entire Pune💕
Lotsa spices and cooked veggies cooked over a huge tawa, with humongous amount of butter in it.😍
Just for the sakes of it, I have included the pictures of the preparation of the very delicious Pav Bhaji, and you can actually see the amount of cheese and butter that goes in to it's making🤩

Served with toasted Pav in butter (I'd rather say deep fried in butter😂)
This was one of the best Pav Bhajis by farr I have had💕

Even if you are not fond of Pav Bhaji, I insist you try it here!!
And may be you would thank me later for suggesting you this place❤
.
.
Ps: Can an extra dollop of butter kill anyone's diet?
When the Pav Bhaji looks sooo yumm?❣️

Pav bhaji is iconic dish from Mumbai but hugely popular all over India..Pav is bread & Bhaji is mashed & spiced vegetables curry..
So to make Pav bhaji - onions , tomatoes , ginger-garlic , capsicum & peas gravy is prepared & you can add all the mashed veggies ( I use potatoes,carrots,cauliflower&cabbage ) followed by ‘pav bhaji masala’ & topped with dollop of butter ..
Street Food Doesn’t get better than this !
It’s spicy , so flavourful & can be easily made VEGAN by replacing with vegan butter..if you never had this in your life , you are seriously missing out something..
It’s one of the street food I can eat everyday without getting bored ever ..It’s so good & yummy how can someone not like it ??
Now when your bhaji is ready , you just need to wait till your PAV is toasted to perfection with oodles of butter!! Squeeze a tad of lemon onto your bhaji & top it with raw onions & forget yourself in this yummy goodness 🧡

Oh.. it was just so perfect! Ah..... The pavbhaji streetstalls of Mumbai have reached  my home,at last!

Tried pav bhaji for the first time . I bought the pav bread but the bhaji is completely homemade. The labour of smashing the veggie gravy  with a traditional wooden smasher was worth it. 
I never knew  the secret behind  pav bhajis rich reddish brown colour was the beet root and  red chilli paste!

Thanks to @yourfoodlab _ Chef Sanjhyot Kheer for the recipie. He is fantastic.. you should try out some of his online recipes, if you are a cooking enthusiast. 
I used homemade garam.masala and dry mango powder instead of store bought pav bhaji masala and the taste was just the same. No compromise.

Gorged pav bhaji for lunch and served it at home. 
Until again! From #ediblechemlab

How to make delicious pav bhaji?

Pav Bhaji is one of the most popular #Indian #snacks, especially in Maharashtra. It is a delicious combination of different vegetables cooked and mashed together. This is one dish, loved by people of all ages and cooked with different variations in different households. #PavBhaji is the smartest way to have all the healthy vegetables together without compromising on the taste. Here is a spicy, easy and low fat Pav Bhaji recipe for you can make anytime. 
Pav Bhaji is an amalgamation of all sorts of healthy vegetables which you might not like when eaten individually.

INGREDIENTS: 
1 tsp Oil
4 cubes Large Butter, finely chopped
1 Cup Onion, chopped
1 tsp Ginger-Garlic paste
1/2 Cup Lauki, chopped
1/2 Cup Capsicum, chopped
1 Cup Potatoes, chopped
1/2 Cup Beetroot, chopped
2 tsp Salt
1 tsp Chili powder
3 tsp Pav Bhaji Masala
1 tsp Red chili powder
1/2 Cup Tomato puree
1 cube to taste Butter
1 Bunch Coriander leaves

-DP’s FAMOUS PAV BHAJI 
We’ve always tried different types of Pav Bhaji at different places. 
Every place calls itself to be famous when it come to Pav Bhaji.
DP’s pav bhaji also flaunts about being famous, wanted and known by celebs.
Honestly, we couldn’t find anything different here. It was the same basic Pav Bhaji that we have at any other place. 
Really disappointing 😟
One of the most different and tasty pav bhaji you can ever have is at ‘Maruti Pav Bhaji’ in Vile Parle. It is famous for its black color pav bhaji and kothumbir Masala Pav. 🤤

How I made the Pav Bhaji: 💚💚Boil peas and finely chopped veggies like potatoes, cauliflower, carrots and green bell pepper in a pressure cooker with salt and some water for 3 whistles and simmer for 15 minutes.Mash the veggies with a potato masher.
💚💚Saute finely chopped onions and fresh crushed garlic and green chilles in oil/ butter( omit the butter if #vegan). 💚💚When the onions are soft add two tablespoons of tomato paste ( the secret of the pretty color) and some fresh tomato puree. 💚💚Add spice powders like turmeric, red chilly/ paprika, corriander and most importantly pav bhaji masala( blend of special spices for pav bhaji). Saute till the masalas are well blended and oil starts leaving the sides of the wok.
💚💚Add the boiled and mashed veggies little by little so as to mix properly. Add salt and water if needed to adjust consistency. 💚💚Add a tablespoon or two of tamarind paste to add some tanginess. Add some chopped cilantro.
💚💚Serve with toasted dinner rolls ( pavs) (adding optional butter and a sprinkle of pav bhaji masala) and chopped cilantro and some chopped onions . Enjoy ! . . .

Pav Bhaji – a spicy curry of mixed vegetables (bhaji) cooked in a special blend of spices and served with soft buttered pav (bread bun shallow fried in butter), is any Indian food lover’s dream. Индийское настроение: паратхи с зеленью и сабджи «пав-бхаджи»(поджаренные картофель, зеленый горошек, цветная капуста в соусе из помидор и множества индийских специй) - очень-очень вкусно, даже сердце застучало от радости встречи со вкусом!
~
Паратхи придумала делать как азербайджанские кутабы - так получается сочнее, т.к. много начинки - очень-очень советую!
~
Даже рецепт напишу:
Тесто:
Муку(вкуснее с индийской Atta - чапатной), чуточку соли и ложку гхи, теплую воду и замешиваем мягкое тесто, на 20 мин убрать в пленку.
~
Любую зелень, у меня была китайская горчица и кориандр(глобально можно любую начинку 😉)- мелко рубим, добавляем специи, соль, можно добавить творог или обычный сыр, но без них тоже вкусно получается!
~
Раскатываем лепешку, кладем начинку, складываем вдвое, защипываем края и жарим на сковороде с маслом, я закрываю крышку и жарю на среднем огне до золотистости с одной стороны, переворачиваю и с другой.
~
Получается обалденно вкусно😋😋!!!

Pav Bhaji
If we are eating out, we consider pav bhaaji as snack, but if we cook bhaaji and bake pav at home, we have this for lunch or dinner!!!
If properly planned you can definitely prepare this wholesome meal at home.... Chop and pack veggies in the fridge previous night. Wash potatoes also previous night, so that in the morning you just have boiling work......... . For buns in a pan keep measured flour, salt and sugar previous night and add rest of the ingredients in the morning..... You can bake buns previous night also, but till next day family members will keep on hogging them... so better bake them fresh😀😀

Asheville’s chefs are redefining Appalachian food with global flavors #FACTS AUG. 14, 2018 In southern #Appalachia — the mountainous region that stretches from #WestVirginia to #Mississippi — the trendiest #food movements are nothing new. #Farmtotable cuisine, whole animal meals and preserved #vegetables are practices that go back generations, to a time when using the local bounty and canning foods throughout the year was done out of necessity, not an evolving public moral consciousness “The types of dishes that you think of that are representative of the area — #leatherbritches which are dried beans which are then cooked, or dried apple snack cake, different kinds of preserves, or using lard and cornmeal and sorghum — it was all based on what’s inexpensive and what’s a way to make it last, to get through the whole year because people were living off the land and they only had what they grew,” chef #KatieButton owner of #Cúrate and #Nightbell in #Asheville #NorthCarolina said

Sitting in the heart of the region, Asheville has risen as Appalachia’s culinary epicenter in recent years. Here, you’ll find the backbone of conventional #Appalachiancuisine hasn’t changed much. At Nightbell, a small-plates restaurant with a focus on local ingredients, Button and her team pickle green garlic and preserve #tomatoes for jam in the summer months. Come fall, they’ll add leather britches to the menu. But Button and other local chefs are also stretching their legs, using local ingredients to infuse #Southern #flavors into global cuisines

Appalachian cuisine itself is a fusion of foods from around the world, chef Meherwan Irani said

In the kitchen at Chai Pani, his Indian street food restaurant, Irani uses local ingredients to shift the boundaries of Indian cuisine. #Kale pakoras and #okrafries julienned and served with a wedge of #lime, are on the menu alongside classic #streetfood like #pavbhaji or #bhelpuri #FOODNINFO #FOODNETWORK #TRUECOOKS #NYC #LAEATS #HUFFPOSTGRAM #TASTY

Pav bhaji! (Pressure cooker recipe) 😍

Ingredients
1 1/2 cups finely chopped tomatoes
1 1/2 cups peeled and chopped potatoes
1/2 cup cauliflower florets
1/2 cup green peas
1 tbsp oil
2 tbsp butter
2 tsp cumin seeds (jeera)
1/2 cup finely chopped onions
1/2 cup chopped capsicum
1 tbsp chilli powder
1 1/2 tbsp pav bhaji masala
salt to taste
2 tbsp finely chopped coriander (dhania) 
For The Garnish
1 cup finely chopped onions
4 lemon wedges
2 tbsp finely chopped coriander (dhania) 
For Serving
10 laddi pavs , buttered and toasted
Method
Heat the oil and butter in the pressure cooker and add the cumin seeds.
When the seeds crackle, add the onions and capsicum sauté on a medium flame for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, potatoes, cauliflower, peas, chilli powder, pav bhaji masala, salt and ¾ cup of hot water, mix well and pressure cook on a high flame for 3 whistles.
Allow the steam to escape using natural release method, (refer handy tip) before opening the lid.
Mash well using a potato masher till smooth, add the coriander and mix well.
Garnish with onions, lemon and coriander and serve immediately with pav. 
Handy tip:
Natural release method: to use this method, remove the pressure cooker from the hot burner and let the pressure drop by cooling down naturally.
It works best for grains and for beans that you might use for salads, as quick-releasing the pressure can cause the beans to split apart.

PAV BHAJI...One of the most popular street foods of India, Pav Bhaji is notorious for being loaded with butter. The common misconception is, the more the butter, the tastier the Bhaji...but I really don't agree with that🤷...you can go ahead and argue with me after you try making this recipe😉, which has zero butter/ghee. I served the Bhaji with store bought Pav since I did not have enough time to make my own bread. Will make whole wheat, simple and easy to follow Pav soon and post the recipe...
✨Recipe✨
Serves 4👥
Ingredients🌱
500g potatoes, washed, boiled and mashed well
2 Kashmiri/byadgi dry red chillies
1 inch ginger
4 cloves garlic
1/2 cup onions, roughly chopped
3 large pulpy tomatoes, roughly chopped
1/4 cup capsicum, finely chopped
1/2 cup cauliflower, grated
1/2 Tbsp garam masala powder
1 Tbsp Pav Bhaji masala powder
1/2 Tbsp black salt/kala namak
1 Tbsp Chaat masala
1 tsp oil
Juice of half a lemon
Salt as needed
1 1/2-2 cups of hot water
1/2 cup frozen peas
Method♨️
🔸Place red chillies, ginger and garlic in a small pan with half a cup of water and simmer for about 10 minutes, till the chillies are soft and swollen. Let cool. Blend along with it's water and onion to a fine paste. 🔸Heat oil in a large frying pan, add the blended paste and cook on medium heat, stirring constantly till the paste begins to leave the sides. 🔸Add capsicum and cauliflower, add a splash of water if needed and cook for about 5 minutes.
🔸Purée the tomatoes and add to the frying pan, cover and let cook, stirring every now and then till the mixture starts to leaves the sides of the pan. 🔸Now add all the masalas, black salt and cook for a couple of minutes. 🔸Add mashed potatoes, peas, hot water and bring to a boil. Switch off heat. Finish with lemon juice and salt.
🔸Lightly grease your pan with oil and warm the bread on both sides. 🔸Serve Pav bhaji with some chopped onions and lemon slice🤗🤗
🔹Note🔹
I have used only 2 red chillies since Pav Bhaji masala powder will contain reasonable amount of chili powder.

Pav Bhaaji for the soul ☔️ It’s the month of Shravan, and it’s time to pull out all the veg recipes in my book. I actually look forward to this month the entire year. The markets are flooded with the tastiest locally grown veggies and I look forward to eating as many as I can ☔️ I like my Bhaaji to be slightly runny. I add less potatoes and a bit more of every other veggie. Add more potatoes if you like it thicker ☔️ I added an outrageous amount of ghee in my pressure cooker and fried off some garlic and red chilli powder for a couple of seconds. I added onions and cooked till they were translucent. I added chopped tomatoes, tomato purée and salt cooked till mushy. I added chopped carrots, cauliflower, potatoes, capsicum and green peas along with Pav Bhaaji masala (Everest). I added water and pressure cooked it all for a couple of whistles. I let the pressure release on its own and mashed the veggies together. I finished with more ghee. Served with butter toasted soft bread, raw onions and a squeeze of lemon ☔️ The rainy rainy weather complemented our meal really well ☔️ #homemade #homecooking #homecookedmeal #homekitchen #homechef #indiankitchen #indianfood #indianfoodbloggers #pavbhaji #foodofinstagram #foodinsta #foodgasm #foodlover #foodblogger #instafood #instagood #instapic #instablogger #cookedwithlove #vegetarian #vegetarianrecipes #loveforcooking #healthyfood #healthylifestyle #healthyeating #healthyliving #foodphotography #foodstagram #30daysofshravan

Living in India, it’s hard not to enjoy its wonderful street food, specially PAV BHAJI! While there’s nothing wrong with having it ONCE in a while, I still prefer to make mine at home. It gives me control over the hygiene, oil/butter, quality of the ingredients and cooking technique. I don’t eat bread normally so having all purpose flour pav once in a while is fine. However, if pav bhaji is something you eat often/if you eat street food often/consume bread often, I’d urge you to use multigrain/homemade bread. Add a side of salad & you’re good to go! .

Happy Sunday Instafamily!! I had the most wonderful experience eating farali/fasting food @achijamulund restaurant yesterday evening on a special invite from the owner ! I had pav bhaji and other snacks from this place several times earlier! But this was a new farali menu that they have launched on the eve of the religious month of Shravan ! They have done a lot of research and finally discovered a new gluten free pav that is also good for during the fasting days ! How cool is that ! The owner says this is the first time in Mumbai that someone is introducing farali pav bhaji !
I have had gluten free bread even in US and even pav/dinner roll but this here was soft melt in the mouth kind of pav and very light too !! I loved the texture and the taste ! My favorite was the farali pav bhaji in frame which I even managed to show live when they were making it ! You can see the recording in my live stories in the profile for the next few hours! This bhaji was made with potatoes and special in house masalas and it was super amazing ! A must try ! I am tempted to start fasting if I can access such yummy food !😂😂😅! So people who are fasting and even those who are not, you can indulge yourself at this place ! Highly recommend!

Masala Pav ka Bhai Masala Bread 😛 trust me it was soooo good 😍
Just make sure u eat this super hot 😘
.
.
.
• Heat Oil, Add Jeera N Hing
• Once Jeera Crackles, Add Chopped Onions and chopped Chillies.
• Saute, Add Capsicum
• Saute Till Onions Turns Golden Brown
• Add Tomatoes, Ginger Garlic Paste
• Salt To Taste
• 5 spoons of water
• Add Masalas - Kashmiri Chilli Powder + Regular Chilli Powder, Pav Bhaji Masala and Garama Masala
• Saute, Let The Whole Mixture Cook Nicly

They say, when you love someone give them what makes them happy. In my case, this makes my husband extremely happy, Pav Bhaji. This is a fast food snacks from India and I am pretty sure this brings him a lot of childhood memories. ✨ This is a very healthy and at the same time dangerous dish. Wanna know why? Scroll down to find out.⤵️ Ingredients: 
Chopped tomato, potato, onions and capsicum
Green peas
Water
Butter (lots of butter🤤)
Salt
Cumin Seeds
Garlic (also best with garlic paste)
Chili powder
Turmeric Powder
Pav Bhaji Masala Powder
Pav / Soft Bread Rolls
Coriander
Slice of lemon

How:
1. In a heated pan, add chopped tomato, washed and pealed potato and green peas, water and salt. Cover and cook for about 15-20 min. or until all vegetables are nicely done.

2. Once all vegetables are cooked, start mashing the vegetables. You may add a little water to make sure its soft and mushy. Also, turn off the flame at this time. Transfer to a different container and continue mashing. 
3. In a pan, heat in a moderate pan with lots of butter. (Like seriously, a good amount of butter)😁 4. Add onions, cumin seeds, garlic and chili powder. And mix until well incorporated. 
5. After a few minutes, take a few of the mixture in a separate container as this will serve as your chutney later on.

6. Add capsicum, turmeric and Pav Bhaji powder. And mix.

7. Once nicely sautéed, add in the mashed vegetables and mix nicely and evenly. 
8. You may also add red food coloring to make it really look street like. 
9. Add salt only if necessary and water to maintain consistency. And simmer in low heat.

10. Lastly, glaze the pav/bread with butter (lots a butter) and heat it in a pan and toast on both sides.

During plating, add a cube of butter, freshly chopped coriander and a slice of lemon on top of the bhaji. Add the pav/bread with the set aside chutney and extra chopped onions.

This is wat I planned for a day out wer I covered the following places

1) #panchampuriwala
It's 150years old n has been managed by 5generations till date. People stand in queue to have food here. I had the special pancham thali which costed Rs.150. They served 5varieties of puri. You cannot share the thali and the quantity is too much for a person to finish. The food was very yummy but on a scale of 5 I would give a 4. 1 deducted for the chaos being an open place n unhygienic place

2) #colaba
V den planned to do some shopping n wat better than dis place to shop for #ornaments or daily wear clothes in Mumbai 
The place is very crowded and u shud b ready to push n be pushed by people around n still manage to get ur eyes n select the ones that u wish to purchase
Most important - U must b a good #bargainer 
3) #marines 
After a tiring day v decided to go, sit n enjoy the breeze at the #queensnecklace 
People usually come der for jogging or just to hang out with frnds

4) #canon pavbhaji 
It's again a #famous place for #pavbhaji n wid dat v ended our day

Pav bhaji is the most common street food of India and I guess almost everybody likes it. It's the most famous Mumbai's street food. It's soft, delicious, buttered covered pav dipped in steaming hot, delicious bhaji takes the food to another level!! .
Bhaji is a combination of many vegetables, cooked with pav bhaji masala and served with a dollop of butter. 
This is truly an innovation that arose out of the necessity of providing a nice hot meal in a hurry and one that tickles the taste buds too. It's one of the few vegetarian dishes which comes to mind when I am in a hurry as it is quick and easy to make.

INDIAN STREET FOOD🌶
.
Pav Bhaji is a popular Indian street food dish - it consists of a thick vegetable curry which is typically eaten on a fried roll/ bread.
It was one of my favourite Indian meals growing up so I decided to make it this evening, with my own Clean Eating by Jay twist...
.
I added Tofu into the vegetable mix for a source of protein - it tasted delicious!
.
What's even better this is so easy to make and fully customisable to suit your tolerance levels with spice and adding any vegetables you may/ may not like.
.
Ingredients
➖Onion & tomato paste - 1 large white onion - finely chopped
- 1 tsp coconut oil - 1/2 can chopped tomatoes - 1/2 tsp turmeric - 1/2 tsp chilli powder - 2 garlic cloves - crushed - salt/pepper
➖Vegetables - 2 cups cauliflower - 1/2 cup peas - 1/2 red pepper - diced - 1/2 yellow pepper - diced - 2 carrots - sliced thinly - 1/2 aubergine - diced
➖1 block Silken tofu
➖3 tsp Pav Bhaji seasoning
📝 Method
1. Create your onion & tomato paste. Heat 1 tsp coconut oil in a pan and gently fry your chopped onion until golden brown. Add the tinned tomatoes and spices and cook for a further 5 minutes.
2. Steam your vegetables in a steamer until soft or alternatively boil in a saucepan for 20-30 mins.
3. Add the vegetables to your onion and tomato paste and heat slowly. Using a potato masher carefully mash the vegetables.
4. Add your silken tofu and continue to mash to remove large lumps.
5. If needed, add a little more tinned tomatoes & water.
6. Add your pav bhaji seasoning, a squeeze of fresh lemon juice, salt/pepper and chopped fresh chillies.
7. Serve hot with freshly toasted rolls or sourdough. Top with chopped onion and coriander👌🏽

We decided to visit Bbq delights, Ibn Batuta and this is our verdict.

The place is well done and the interiors give a traditional feel with a modern touch. The staff are friendly and welcoming.

We tried Reshmi kabab,ginger chicken, naan, mango juice and orange juice.

Reshmi kabab: juicy, large portion, very well marinated and well cooked. Deserves a 5*. Ginger chicken: this one was also perfectly made and tasted delicious. but, it was a bit dry for our liking. Maybe, a bit more gravy will make the curry more enjoyable, otherwise it becomes too dry with naan. 4*

Naan: usual naan. 1 naan is sufficient for one person.

Mango and orange juice: both were perfectly made (in front of us) using fresh fruits. Chilled and refreshing. We got buy one get one offer for this.

Chutneys, yoghurt,salad, and even green chillis were provided along side.

What we hated about the place:
The place dint have any hand wash area

Perfect place. Would like to come back and try their buffet and business lunch deals.
